bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the legacy Rucio WebUI account-identity table. A privileged attacker can use Admin > Account Management > an account > Add Account Identity (POST /proxy/accounts/<account>/identities) to persist an identity such as <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>. When a victim opens /ui/account?account=<account>, load_identities() obtains the stored identity through r.list_identities() and used to pass the returned objects directly to jQuery DataTables as `data: data`; the `identity` and `type` columns were therefore rendered as HTML rather than output-encoded text. JavaScript executes in the WebUI origin with the viewing user's authority, permitting token/cookie theft or authenticated actions. The closing change constructs a separate display object and HTML-encodes identity/type with `$('<div>').text(String(value)).html()` while retaining raw `$identity`/`$type` only for API operations.
flaw_origin: Commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 (`[RUCIO-2849] RucioUI account admin pages`) is the smallest public first-writer. It created lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js and the account page, adding both the identity creation flow and load_identities(), whose DataTable consumed the server-returned identity objects without encoding. It is a normal one-parent feature commit, not a move, revert, release/backport, merge wrapper, or reconstructable squash; its parent had the identity-list API client but no account page, identities table, or vulnerable display sink.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78` identifies both author and committer as Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch> and contains only the subject `[RUCIO-2849] RucioUI account admin pages`; there is no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, bot identity, AI tool name, or other AI-attribution trailer in the BIC commit object.
evidence:
Advisory identity and lifecycle: the assigned first-party GHSA-8wpv-6x3f-3rm5 / CVE-2026-25735 describes POST /proxy/accounts/pentest/identities with an identity `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` and triggering it at /ui/account?account=pentest. It declares rucio-webui vulnerable at <35.8.3, >=36.0.0rc1,<38.5.4, and >=39.0.0rc1,<39.3.1, with patched versions 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1.

BIC reproduction in /home/hanqing/agents/ai-slop/.ai-slop/state/repos/rucio_rucio: `git log -L 124,158:lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js d1552e23aaeaef108b568edb6af8facf701954ab` traces the vulnerable `load_identities()` block back to 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 and shows that commit adding `dt_ids = $('#identities_table').DataTable({ data: data, ... columns: [{'data': 'identity'}, {'data': 'type'}] })`. The only later history in that line trace before the security series is 45cb01ca08ed60ee66c65618a64b73e16f4aad09, which merely changes the unrelated missing-account message from `.html()` to `.text()` and leaves `data: data` intact. `git log --all -S"data: data" -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` independently reports 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 as the addition and the five 2026 branch copies of the DataTable fix as removals. `git show --stat --summary 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78` shows a one-parent feature commit creating account.js and account.html; no prior file was renamed.

Direct parent absence: `git diff 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js lib/rucio/web/ui/templates/account.html` reports both files as new and shows the vulnerable identity DataTable and add_identity() flow being added. `git grep -n -e list_identities -e identities_table 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e -- lib/rucio/web/ui` finds only the pre-existing rucio.js API client at line 119 and no identities table/rendering sink. Thus the immediate parent lacks the vulnerable lines and behavior. `git cat-file commit 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78` gives parent 797c3fc45a10cba0ffb391d0fa1368857c74cc9e and the exact human-only commit object quoted in ai_marker. GitHub's first-party `GET /repos/rucio/rucio/commits/4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78/pulls` returns an empty array, providing no member history to decompose and agreeing with treating the local atomic first-writer rather than inventing a squash decomposition.

Initial release boundary: `git tag --contains 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 | sort -V` begins with 1.13.3. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78 1.13.2^{}` exits 1, while the same command against 1.13.3^{} exits 0, so 1.13.3 is the first tagged release containing this WebUI sink and 1.13.2 does not contain it. This is consistent with the advisory's open lower bound `<35.8.3`.

Fix and patched-release boundaries: canonical merged master commit b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 (`fix(WebUI): fix XSS using DataTable`, PR #8406) directly replaces raw identity/type display values in account.js with encoded display values and preserves separate raw `$identity`/`$type` fields for deletion. `git diff b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25^ b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` displays that exact hunk; `git grep -n 'data: data' 75a9c1349bdb45b02527108d5fafcecedc9dcafe -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` confirms its direct parent still has the raw DataTable source. The corresponding branch-applied direct copies are a3618f46cde422d762e0bca8ffa219cfe7703003 for 35.8.3, abf5e978ee3910590a23c6705e6a0105c0b847c7 for 38.5.4, and 80b91dd0c6737b2ab9aed039470e8e81028def41 for 39.3.1; `git log 35.8.2..35.8.3 -- account.js`, `git log 38.5.3..38.5.4 -- account.js`, and `git log 39.3.0..39.3.1 -- account.js` identify those commits. Finally, `git grep -n -e sanitisedData -e 'data: data' 35.8.2 35.8.3 38.5.3 38.5.4 39.3.0 39.3.1 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/static/account.js` shows raw `data: data` in all three immediately preceding tags and `sanitisedData` in all three first-patched tags. `git tag --contains b96c1feee372b285c1db881db5bc297a40645b25` includes 40.0.0rc1 and later master-line releases, explaining why the advisory has no vulnerable 40.x range.
reasoning: The vulnerability-first trace identifies a concrete stored-XSS sink, follows it to the first commit that created the account identity page, directly verifies absence in that commit's parent, and verifies both the canonical direct repair and every advisory-listed release boundary. The BIC is 4f67434304e5bd445c01a636d88113b76a68ef78, not any later move/refactor/backport and not the 2026 fix series. AI classification is restricted to that BIC's commit object as required: it is a 2017 commit authored and committed by a named human and carries no AI attribution or bot marker. Later security-fix authorship and PR material are irrelevant to BIC attribution. Therefore the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
